title: Gujarat's Swaminarayan
hook: a sadhu sings his teacher from head to foot, and the song is still sung after the evening lamps

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gujarat's Swaminarayan: satsang, the company of the true. Did you spend time with the person whose company makes you better? Day one thousand four hundred five.

A harmonium, a pair of small cymbals, a handful of voices in a mandir after the evening lamps are done. The song they're singing is a kind of portrait. It moves slowly over one person, the way an eye moves over a face it loves: the forehead, the eyes, the smile, the hands, the feet. The man who first sang it wasn't a painter. He was a sadhu, one of a circle of poets who traveled with Swaminarayan and turned what they saw into songs. Today, our last day in Gujarat: the poet-sadhus, and the songs they left behind.
screen: `AFTER THE EVENING LAMPS.` → `A PORTRAIT IN A SONG.` → `A CIRCLE OF POETS.`

segments.voice: Tradition remembers several of these poets by name. Muktanand Swami, the elder disciple who welcomed Nilkanth at Loj. Brahmanand Swami. Premanand Swami, a singer and musician. Nishkulanand Swami, who also told his teacher's life in the Bhaktachintamani. Their songs are still sung in Swaminarayan mandirs and homes. Look first at the songs of watching. Tradition says Premanand sang Swaminarayan's form from head to foot, and sang the shape of his day as well: how he rose, how he bathed, how he sat with the people who came to see him. Devotees sing songs like these at night, so the day ends with the teacher close. A life remembered in loving detail becomes something to hold. Then the songs of longing. Some are sung in the voice of a devotee who misses the beloved and can't bear the distance. Longing isn't treated as a failure of faith. It's part of love, and the poets give it a tune. Then the songs of letting go. Nishkulanand's verses press on vairagya, detachment. In paraphrase, one of them says that giving things up doesn't hold unless detachment has reached the heart. You can leave a house and still live in it in your mind. Now set these beside the rest of the week. The Vachanamrut gave questions and answers. The Shikshapatri gave a letter for every morning. Satsang gave a company. The poet-sadhus gave something a child can learn by heart: a tune that carries the teacher's face and the teaching together. And that's where Gujarat leaves us: a boy on the road, a new name, a courtyard of questions, a letter, a company, and a circle of poets singing what they saw. What do you know by heart about someone you love?
screen: `THE POET-SADHUS` · `SONGS OF WATCHING` · `SONGS OF LONGING` · `SONGS OF LETTING GO`

segments.voice: A portrait, sung in silence. Sit, and let the breath slow. Bring to mind someone you love, living or gone, or, if you pray, the form of God you pray to. Let your attention move over them slowly, the way the song moves: the forehead, the eyes, the way they smile, their hands. One detail for each breath. Don't hurry to the end. When the mind wanders, come back to the last detail you saw. The bell holds the time.
Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, the poet-sadhus who walked with him, and their songs of watching, longing and letting go. Today's word.
Your line: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, tell someone one small thing you've noticed and love about them, in plain words. Day one thousand four hundred five.
